# Agentic SDLC Framework (Claude Code)

A generic framework that turns a user story into a reviewed, verified pull request. The main Claude Code session acts as the **Orchestrator** and delegates to eight specialist subagents. It is not tied to any application, language or stack. `CLAUDE.md` holds the project-wide instructions; details are in `.claude/rules/`.

## Expense Tracker application (generated by this workflow)

A single-user, local-only web app for recording, listing, filtering, editing and deleting personal expenses (Flask + SQLite). It binds to `127.0.0.1` only, with debug off.

### Install
```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt   # Windows (Git Bash)
# Linux/macOS: .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
```
`requirements.txt` holds the runtime dependency (Flask); `requirements-dev.txt` adds pytest and pip-audit.

### Run
```bash
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/Scripts/python -m expense_tracker            # http://127.0.0.1:5000/
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/Scripts/python -m expense_tracker --port 8123
```
The package is not installed into the environment, so `PYTHONPATH=src` (PowerShell: `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"`) is required. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.
The database file is created on first start. Set `EXPENSE_DB_PATH` to choose its location (default `data/expenses.db`, git-ignored):
```bash
PYTHONPATH=src EXPENSE_DB_PATH=/path/to/expenses.db .venv/Scripts/python -m expense_tracker
```
Only `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` Host headers are accepted. Host and debug mode cannot be configured.

### Test
```bash
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest
```

### Categories
Food, Transport, Housing, Utilities, Entertainment, Health, Shopping, Other.

### Privacy and logging
Expense data is stored only in the local SQLite file. Logs are minimal: on failure only the operation name and exception class are written, never amounts, descriptions, request data, file paths, messages or tracebacks (see `docs/decisions/0004-log-content-policy.md`).

### Known limitations
- "Today" (used to reject future expense dates) is the server machine's local date; there is no time zone handling.
- Logs are intentionally minimal, so diagnosing failures may need a debugger or a reproduction.
- Single user, no authentication; do not expose the port beyond the local machine.

## Architecture

```text
Human <-> Orchestrator (main session: CLAUDE.md + rules + skills)
              | one stage at a time, with an explicit handoff packet
              v
 requirements -> architecture -> design review -> planning
 -> implementation -> code review -> verification -> PR
```

- No Orchestrator subagent exists. Specialists never delegate to each other; they return a structured report.
- Subagents do not share context. The Orchestrator passes artifact paths, approvals and quoted decisions.
- Progress is tracked in `docs/workflow-state.md`, so a workflow can be resumed.

## Agents (`.claude/agents/`)

| Agent | Responsibility | Produces | Tools |
|-------|----------------|----------|-------|
| `requirements-agent` | Analyze story, find gaps, raise questions | `docs/requirements.md` | Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob |
| `architecture-agent` | Choose stack, design components/data/APIs | `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/decisions/*` | Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob |
| `design-review-agent` | Independent architecture review | `docs/design-review.md` | Read, Write, Grep, Glob |
| `planning-agent` | Ordered, traceable tasks; never codes | `docs/impl-plan.md` | Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob |
| `implementation-agent` | Code and tests on `development` | `src/`, `tests/`, local commits | + Bash |
| `code-review-agent` | Independent review, severity-classified | `docs/code-review.md` | Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash (read-only use) |
| `verification-agent` | Runs tests, checks ACs with evidence | `docs/verification-report.md` | Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash |
| `pr-agent` | Prepares PR; submits only with approval; never merges | `output/pr-description.md`, the PR | Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash |

Tool lists are least-privilege; path limits (such as "reviewers write only their report") are enforced by agent instructions and the Orchestrator's checks.

## Skills and slash commands (`.claude/skills/`)

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `/start-sdlc [Jira key \| story path \| resume]` | Entry point: runs or resumes the whole workflow |
| `/analyze-requirements` | Requirements, clarification, gate G1 |
| `/design-architecture` | Architecture and gate G2 |
| `/review-design` | Independent design review and resolution |
| `/create-implementation-plan` | Task plan |
| `/implement-feature [TASK-### \| FND-###]` | Implement tasks or fix findings on `development` |
| `/review-code` | Code review, fix and re-review loop |
| `/verify-application` | Test execution and AC verification |
| `/prepare-pr` | Readiness check, PR draft, gate G3, submission |

Stage skills are also usable on their own to re-run a single stage. All are user-invoked only (`disable-model-invocation`).

## Shared instructions (`.claude/rules/`)
`general.md`, `git-workflow.md`, `security.md`, `agent-orchestration.md` always load. `testing.md` and `documentation.md` load only when working on matching paths (`paths:` frontmatter).

## Hooks (`.claude/hooks/`, configured in `.claude/settings.json`)

| Hook | Event | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| `guard-bash.sh` | PreToolUse (Bash) | Blocks force-push, push to `main`, switching to `main`, `reset --hard`, `clean`, branch deletion, `--no-verify`, `rm -rf`, reading `.env`, and commit/merge/rebase while on `main` |
| `guard-write.sh` | PreToolUse (Write, Edit) | Blocks writing `.env` files (not `.env.example`) and writing `src/` or `tests/` unless on `development` |
| `session-start.sh` | SessionStart | Prints current branch and workflow stage |

Limitations: hooks match command text with simple patterns and cannot see intent. Approval gates, "preserve unrelated changes" and "only write your own artifact" are enforced by agent instructions, not hooks. Remote branch protection must be set on the hosting platform. Hooks need `bash` (Git Bash on Windows).

## Branching
- `main`: protected; no direct commits, pushes or merges by agents. Changes arrive only through an approved PR.
- `development`: the only working branch; all code and commits. No feature branches.
- PR: `development` -> `main`, created by `pr-agent` only after explicit approval. The user merges.

## Approval gates
1. **G1**: requirements approved, before architecture.
2. **G2**: architecture and ADRs approved, before design review and planning. Reopened by any architecture change.
3. **G3**: before pushing `development` and creating the PR.

Review and verification findings go back to the responsible agent until checks pass (escalated after three rounds).

## Getting started
1. Check out `development` (create it first if missing; agents will not).
2. Run `/start-sdlc` and give it a Jira key (needs the Jira MCP configured), a path to a story file, or paste the story. Use `/start-sdlc resume` to continue.
3. Answer clarification questions and approve at G1, G2 and G3.

### Providing a new user story
Put the story and acceptance criteria in `docs/user-story.md`, or paste them to `/start-sdlc`. To begin a different story after a completed workflow, run `/start-sdlc` again and confirm replacing the previous workflow; history stays in git. Keep acceptance criteria concrete and testable.

## Repository structure
```text
.claude/agents/   Specialist agent definitions
.claude/skills/   Slash-command workflows (one folder per skill, SKILL.md)
.claude/rules/    Shared and path-scoped instructions
.claude/hooks/    Hook scripts (wired in settings.json)
docs/             Workflow artifacts and state
src/, tests/      Application code and tests, generated per story
output/           Generated output (git-ignored)
CLAUDE.md         Project-wide instructions
```
